Two years ago, Sonos expanded from the wireless speaker market into the over-ear headphone space. Now, Sonos appears poised to launch a next-generation successor positioned higher up the range, featuring artificial intelligence technology.

The Sonos Ace Ultra over-ear headphones are about to debut

Chris Welch reports for Bloomberg that Sonos is developing the Sonos Ace Ultra, an upgraded successor to the 2024 Ace headphones.

An application document disclosed on Monday by the U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) mentions the product name and indicates up to five colour options — an increase from the original model's two colours of black and white.

Sonos plans to hold a product launch event in September. According to the filing's timeline, the Ace Ultra may be one of the products unveiled on that day.

The filing also contains technical clues, suggesting the new headphones may support voice command functionality.

Bloomberg reports that CEO Tom Conrad has acknowledged that the original headphones lacked sufficient whole-home integration capabilities when launched, and failed to carve out a clear distinction in the fiercely competitive market for similar products.

This time, Sonos appears intent on integrating its hardware more directly into a broader artificial intelligence strategy.

Conrad has positioned the company's growth opportunities around conversational computing and predictive intelligence for the home environment, framing Sonos devices as hardware capable of operating across rooms and understanding household living patterns.

The company has expanded Sonos Voice Control to support Philips Hue and Lutron Caseta.

Meanwhile, Apple's upgraded AirPods Max 2 launched in March, equipped with the H2 chip, stronger noise cancellation, and real-time translation capabilities. Siri artificial intelligence will extend to AirPods via iOS 27.

For details on the upcoming Sonos Ace Ultra over-ear headphones, refer to the full Bloomberg report.
